correctness.rationale: The dual of a bounded chain C_{a_i+1} is an a_i-point chain; the dual of the product is their disjoint union. Full bi-Heyting homomorphisms are precisely inverses of maps satisfying both the upward and downward bounded-morphism identities. An isotone map sends each source chain into one connected target chain; the two lifting conditions force a surjection onto its entire target component. Conversely every isotone chain-surjection satisfies both liftings. Ordered positive fiber compositions give w_ij=binom(a_i-1,a_j-1). Independent source-component choices prove the product cardinality. Inclusion-exclusion over missed targets gives E_J. Idempotence forces identity on occupied components and unrestricted maps from unoccupied ones, giving I_J. Any shortest-length source demands a shortest-length target; for sufficiency keep all occupied targets fixed and map remaining sources onto such a shortest target. The algebraic image has cardinality product_{j in J}(a_j+1), since it is the upset algebra of the full dual image. This proves the two polynomials, equal-length Stirling specialization and positivity cutoff for all k>=1, a_i>=1; supports yielding the same numeric cardinality aggregate coefficients. Independently enumerated all 31 ordered length vectors with sum<=5 and 3970 valid dual self-morphisms, agreeing with support and idempotent counts. Source script independently checked larger finite domains but is not relied on for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Finite products of bi-Gödel chains are canonical models of finite co-forest bi-Heyting algebras. An exact two-variable distinction between endomorphism and retract image-size distributions is a natural structural invariant with concrete algebraic uses, and simultaneous support feasibility for both map types is a non-obvious common spectrum. Heterogeneous multiplicities and collisions of cardinalities are not elementary Boolean function counting; the formulas solve a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary small slice. They do not claim a new duality theorem.
